STEM.label: STEM
STEM.description: Science, technology, engineering, math, and computing

Health.label: Health & Medicine
Health.description: Biomedical research, health careers, and wellness

Business.label: Business & Entrepreneurship
Business.description: Startups, finance, economics, and career organizations

Arts.label: Arts & Media
Arts.description: Visual art, writing, music, theater, film, and journalism

Civics.label: Civics & Leadership
Civics.description: Government, law, debate, public service, and global affairs

Scholarships.label: Scholarships & College Access
Scholarships.description: Money for college and free college-prep support

opportunities.title: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
opportunities.costNote: Small entry fees; fee waivers for students with financial need; scholarships for top winners
opportunities.description: The longest-running recognition program for creative teens in grades 7-12, with categories from painting and photography to poetry, journalism, and video games. National Medalists are celebrated in New York.

opportunities.title: National Student Poets Program
opportunities.organization: Institute of Museum and Library Services & Alliance for Young Artists & Writers
opportunities.costNote: Selected from Scholastic Awards poetry winners; includes an academic award
opportunities.deadline: Enter through the Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
opportunities.description: The nation's highest honor for youth poets. Five students are chosen each year to serve as literary ambassadors, leading poetry projects in their regions.

opportunities.title: YoungArts National Arts Competition
opportunities.costNote: Application fee with waivers available; cash awards for winners
opportunities.description: For artists ages 15-18 in visual, literary, design, and performing arts. Winners receive cash awards, mentorship from leading artists, and are eligible for nomination as U.S. Presidential Scholars in the Arts.

opportunities.title: Congressional Art Competition
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter
opportunities.description: Each spring, members of Congress host a visual art competition in their districts. The winning artwork from each district hangs in the U.S. Capitol for a year.

opportunities.title: Poetry Out Loud
opportunities.organization: National Endowment for the Arts & Poetry Foundation
opportunities.costNote: Free; cash prizes at state and national levels
opportunities.description: National poetry recitation contest. Students memorize and perform great poems, advancing from classroom and school contests to state and national championships.

opportunities.title: New York Times Learning Network Student Contests
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter
opportunities.deadline: Contests run throughout the school year
opportunities.description: Year-round contests for students ages 13-19 in personal narrative, editorial writing, reviews, podcasting, photography, and more. Winners are published by The New York Times.

opportunities.title: NPR Student Podcast Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter
opportunities.description: Students create a short podcast on any topic, typically with a teacher sponsor. Winning entries are featured on NPR programs.

opportunities.title: Adroit Journal Summer Mentorship Program
opportunities.costNote: Free online mentorship
opportunities.description: Free online creative writing mentorship where high school students work one-on-one with published writers in poetry or prose over the summer.

opportunities.title: Iowa Young Writers' Studio
opportunities.costNote: Tuition with need-based scholarships
opportunities.description: Summer creative writing program for high school students, run by the home of the famous Iowa Writers' Workshop, with residential and online sessions.

opportunities.title: Bennington Young Writers Awards
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; cash prizes
opportunities.description: Writing competition for high school students in poetry, fiction, and nonfiction, judged by Bennington College faculty and students.

opportunities.title: Write the World Competitions
opportunities.costNote: Free to join and enter
opportunities.description: Online writing community for ages 13-19 with monthly genre competitions, peer review, and feedback from expert writers.

opportunities.title: Ocean Awareness Contest
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; cash awards
opportunities.description: Students ages 11-18 create art, poetry, prose, film, music, or advocacy projects about the ocean and climate, competing for cash awards.

opportunities.title: Interlochen Arts Camp
opportunities.costNote: Tuition with need-based and merit scholarships
opportunities.description: Renowned summer arts camp with intensive programs in music, theatre, dance, visual arts, creative writing, and film for students in grades 3-12.

opportunities.title: National Youth Orchestra of the USA (NYO-USA)
opportunities.costNote: Free, including travel
opportunities.description: Each summer, top young musicians ages 16-19 train with professional orchestra musicians, then perform at Carnegie Hall and tour internationally.

opportunities.title: NYO2
opportunities.costNote: Free, including travel
opportunities.description: Summer orchestral training program for musicians ages 14-17, with a focus on students from communities underserved in classical music.

opportunities.title: From the Top
opportunities.costNote: Free; selected performers receive scholarship awards
opportunities.description: National nonprofit that celebrates young classical musicians ages 8-18 through its radio show, performances, and fellowships that develop artistic leadership.

opportunities.title: Essentially Ellington
opportunities.location: Online submission; finals in New York
opportunities.costNote: Free for high school jazz bands
opportunities.description: High school jazz band program and competition. Bands receive free Duke Ellington charts and feedback, and finalists perform at Jazz at Lincoln Center.

opportunities.title: NAfME All-National Honor Ensembles
opportunities.costNote: Audition and participation fees
opportunities.description: Top high school musicians are selected by audition for national honor ensembles (band, orchestra, choir, jazz, and guitar) that rehearse and perform together.

opportunities.title: Boston University Tanglewood Institute
opportunities.costNote: Tuition with need-based and merit aid
opportunities.description: Summer music training for young musicians at Tanglewood, the summer home of the Boston Symphony Orchestra, with orchestra, voice, and composition programs.

opportunities.title: RISD Pre-College
opportunities.costNote: Tuition with need-based scholarships
opportunities.description: Intensive summer program for students ages 16-18 to study art and design at college level, explore a major, and build a portfolio.

opportunities.title: Pratt Institute PreCollege
opportunities.costNote: Tuition with scholarships available
opportunities.description: Summer art, design, architecture, and creative writing intensives in Brooklyn where students earn college credit and develop portfolio work.

opportunities.title: NYU Tisch Summer High School Programs
opportunities.organization: NYU Tisch School of the Arts
opportunities.costNote: Tuition with limited scholarships
opportunities.description: Four-week residential pre-college program for rising sophomores and juniors. Students choose one track, such as filmmaking, acting, dance, game design, or photography, and earn NYU college credit.

opportunities.title: California State Summer School for the Arts (CSSSA)
opportunities.costNote: Subsidized tuition for California residents with need-based aid
opportunities.description: Four-week pre-professional arts training in animation, creative writing, dance, film, music, theater, and visual arts for talented California students.

opportunities.title: Doodle for Google
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; scholarship for the national winner
opportunities.description: K-12 students design a Google logo around a yearly theme. The national winner's doodle appears on Google's homepage and earns a college scholarship.

opportunities.title: All American High School Film Festival
opportunities.location: Online submission; festival in New York
opportunities.costNote: Submission fee; prizes and scholarships for winners
opportunities.description: The largest film festival for high school filmmakers. Students submit short films for screening, awards, and scholarship opportunities.

opportunities.title: Kenyon Review Young Writers Workshops
opportunities.costNote: Tuition with need-based scholarships
opportunities.description: Creative writing workshops for high school students led by published writers, offered as a two-week residential program at Kenyon College and shorter online sessions, with need-based aid for every format.

opportunities.title: Future Business Leaders of America (FBLA)
opportunities.costNote: Membership dues through your school chapter
opportunities.description: The largest business career student organization. Members build leadership skills and compete in events in accounting, marketing, public speaking, coding, and entrepreneurship.

opportunities.title: DECA
opportunities.costNote: Membership dues through your school chapter
opportunities.description: Prepares emerging leaders in marketing, finance, hospitality, and management through role-play competitions, business plans, and conferences up to the International Career Development Conference.

opportunities.title: Business Professionals of America (BPA)
opportunities.costNote: Membership dues through your school chapter
opportunities.description: Career and technical student organization for business management, IT, finance, and office careers, with workplace skills competitions at regional, state, and national levels.

opportunities.title: JA Company Program
opportunities.costNote: Free through schools and local JA offices
opportunities.deadline: Offered through schools and local JA areas
opportunities.description: Students launch and run a real business from idea to liquidation with a volunteer mentor, learning product development, marketing, and finance along the way.

opportunities.title: Diamond Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; prize money for winning teams
opportunities.description: Global entrepreneurship competition for teams of high school students ages 14-18. Teams pitch a business or social innovation concept for a chance at prize money and a trip to the summit.

opportunities.title: Wharton Global High School Investment Competition
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter
opportunities.description: Teams of high school students manage a virtual investment portfolio for a client case, then write and present an investment strategy. Top teams compete at the global finale.

opportunities.title: NFTE World Series of Innovation
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; cash prizes for winners
opportunities.description: Young people ages 13-24 submit innovative product or service ideas tied to the UN Sustainable Development Goals and partner company challenges.

opportunities.title: National Economics Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter
opportunities.description: Team academic competition testing knowledge of microeconomics, macroeconomics, and current events. Top teams advance to the national finals.

opportunities.title: National Personal Finance Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter
opportunities.description: Teams demonstrate personal finance knowledge (budgeting, credit, saving, investing, and taxes) through tests and a case study, competing from state to national level.

opportunities.title: The Stock Market Game
opportunities.costNote: Usually free or low cost through participating teachers
opportunities.description: Online simulation where student teams invest a virtual portfolio in real markets, learning about investing, saving, and the economy. Usually joined through a teacher.

opportunities.title: High School Fed Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter
opportunities.description: Teams act as the Federal Reserve's policy committee, analyzing economic conditions and presenting a monetary policy recommendation to a panel of Fed economists.

opportunities.title: Young Entrepreneurs Academy (YEA!)
opportunities.costNote: Tuition varies; scholarships often available
opportunities.description: Year-long program where students ages 11-18 start real businesses or social movements, pitch to investors, and learn from local business mentors.

opportunities.title: LaunchX Entrepreneurship Programs
opportunities.costNote: Tuition-based with need-based financial aid
opportunities.deadline: Rolling admissions in winter and spring
opportunities.description: Summer entrepreneurship programs where student teams identify a real problem, build a startup around it, and pitch to investors and founders at the end.

opportunities.title: Economics for Leaders
opportunities.costNote: Tuition with scholarships available
opportunities.description: One-week summer program that teaches economic reasoning and leadership skills through simulations, lectures, and group activities on college campuses.

opportunities.title: Blue Ocean Entrepreneurship Competition
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; cash prizes
opportunities.description: Global pitch competition for high school students using Blue Ocean Strategy: students submit a short video pitch for an innovative idea that creates new market space.

opportunities.title: Family, Career and Community Leaders of America (FCCLA)
opportunities.costNote: Membership dues through your school chapter
opportunities.description: Career and technical student organization focused on family and consumer sciences careers, including culinary arts, hospitality, early childhood education, and fashion.

opportunities.title: United States Senate Youth Program
opportunities.costNote: All expenses paid plus a college scholarship
opportunities.description: Two students from each state who serve in an elected or appointed student leadership office spend a week in Washington meeting senators, cabinet officials, and Supreme Court justices, and receive a college scholarship.

opportunities.title: U.S. Senate Page Program
opportunities.costNote: Paid position; housing provided for a fee
opportunities.description: High school juniors who are at least 16 serve as pages on the Senate floor, attend the Senate Page School, and see the legislative process up close. Appointments are made by sponsoring senators.

opportunities.title: The Congressional Award
opportunities.costNote: One-time registration fee; waivers available
opportunities.description: Congress's award for young Americans ages 14-24. Participants set and achieve goals in volunteer service, personal development, physical fitness, and expedition to earn certificates and medals.

opportunities.title: American Legion Boys State
opportunities.costNote: Usually sponsored by local Legion posts
opportunities.description: Week-long program where rising seniors build a mock state government, run for office, and pass legislation. Two delegates from each state go on to Boys Nation in Washington, DC.

opportunities.title: American Legion Auxiliary Girls State
opportunities.costNote: Usually sponsored by local Auxiliary units
opportunities.description: Week-long leadership program where rising seniors learn how government works by running for office and governing a mock state. Two delegates per state go on to Girls Nation.

opportunities.title: YMCA Youth & Government
opportunities.costNote: Program fees vary by state; scholarships often available
opportunities.description: Students serve as legislators, lobbyists, attorneys, judges, and journalists in a model state government, culminating in a session at the state capitol.

opportunities.title: Close Up Washington Programs
opportunities.costNote: Program fee with need-based fellowships
opportunities.description: Week-long civic education trips to Washington, DC, where students meet with members of Congress, debate policy issues, and study government at monuments and memorials.

opportunities.title: Junior State of America (JSA)
opportunities.costNote: Chapter dues; summer schools charge tuition with aid
opportunities.description: Student-run organization for political debate and civic engagement, with chapter conventions and summer schools at universities focused on government and leadership.

opportunities.title: National Speech & Debate Association
opportunities.costNote: Membership through your school team
opportunities.description: The national honor society and league for speech and debate, with events like policy, Lincoln-Douglas, public forum, congressional debate, and original oratory.

opportunities.title: Model United Nations
opportunities.costNote: Conference fees vary
opportunities.description: Students represent countries in simulated UN committees, researching global issues, negotiating, and drafting resolutions at conferences hosted by schools and universities.

opportunities.title: National History Day
opportunities.costNote: Small contest fees vary by state
opportunities.description: Year-long research program where students create papers, exhibits, documentaries, performances, or websites on a historical topic tied to an annual theme.

opportunities.title: We the People: The Citizen and the Constitution
opportunities.costNote: Offered through participating teachers
opportunities.description: Classes study the Constitution and Bill of Rights, then compete in simulated congressional hearings in front of judges, advancing from state to national finals.

opportunities.title: National High School Mock Trial Championship
opportunities.organization: National High School Mock Trial Championship
opportunities.costNote: Fees vary by state program
opportunities.description: Teams act as attorneys and witnesses in a simulated trial judged by real attorneys and judges, advancing from state championships to the national championship.

opportunities.title: National High School Ethics Bowl
opportunities.organization: Parr Center for Ethics, UNC Chapel Hill
opportunities.costNote: Usually free for teams
opportunities.description: A collaborative discussion competition where teams analyze real ethical dilemmas and are judged on the quality of their reasoning, not on beating opponents.

opportunities.title: C-SPAN StudentCam
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; cash prizes
opportunities.description: National video documentary competition for students in grades 6-12. Students create short documentaries on a yearly civics theme for cash prizes and a chance to air on C-SPAN.

opportunities.title: JFK Profile in Courage Essay Contest
opportunities.organization: John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; cash awards for winners
opportunities.description: Students write an essay about an act of political courage by a U.S. elected official since 1917. Winners receive cash awards and are honored at the Kennedy Library.

opportunities.title: Telluride Association Summer Seminar (TASS)
opportunities.costNote: Free, including tuition, housing, and travel
opportunities.description: Free six-week college-level seminar in the humanities and social sciences focused on critical Black studies and anti-oppressive studies, with no grades or credit, just learning.

opportunities.title: HOBY State Leadership Seminars
opportunities.costNote: Fees are often covered by schools or sponsors
opportunities.description: Multi-day leadership seminars for high school sophomores focused on personal leadership, group collaboration, and community service, followed by a service commitment.

opportunities.title: Running Start Young Women's Political Leadership Program
opportunities.costNote: Free, with travel and lodging covered
opportunities.description: Week-long program in Washington, DC that introduces high school young women to political leadership through workshops with elected officials and campaign experts.

opportunities.title: National Security Language Initiative for Youth (NSLI-Y)
opportunities.costNote: Merit-based scholarship covering travel, tuition, and homestay
opportunities.description: Full scholarships for students ages 15-18 to learn critical languages such as Arabic, Chinese, Korean, Russian, or Turkish through summer or academic-year programs abroad.

opportunities.title: Congress-Bundestag Youth Exchange (CBYX)
opportunities.costNote: Full scholarship for a year in Germany
opportunities.description: Scholarship for students ages 15-18.5 to spend an academic year in Germany living with a host family and attending a German high school.

opportunities.title: Kennedy-Lugar YES Abroad
opportunities.costNote: Full scholarship for an academic year abroad
opportunities.description: Merit-based scholarships for U.S. students ages 15-18.5 to spend an academic year in countries with significant Muslim populations, living with a host family.

opportunities.title: U.S. Presidential Scholars Program
opportunities.costNote: Honor by invitation only; students cannot apply on their own
opportunities.description: One of the nation's highest honors for graduating high school seniors, recognizing academic, artistic, and career and technical achievement.

opportunities.title: West Point Summer Leaders Experience
opportunities.costNote: Program fee with financial assistance available
opportunities.description: Week-long program for high school juniors to experience academics, military training, and athletics at West Point.

opportunities.title: U.S. Naval Academy Summer Seminar
opportunities.costNote: Program fee with financial assistance available
opportunities.description: Week-long program for rising seniors to experience life as a midshipman, with academic workshops, leadership training, and physical fitness.

opportunities.title: American Legion Oratorical Contest
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; college scholarships for winners
opportunities.description: Students deliver a prepared speech on the U.S. Constitution and an assigned topic, competing from local and state levels to national finals for college scholarships.

opportunities.title: Educators Rising
opportunities.costNote: Membership through your school chapter
opportunities.description: Career organization for high school students interested in becoming teachers, with hands-on teaching experience, competitions, and a national conference.

opportunities.title: Student Poll Worker Programs
opportunities.organization: U.S. Election Assistance Commission & local election offices
opportunities.costNote: Poll workers are usually paid; many states accept workers ages 16-17
opportunities.description: Many states allow high school students to serve as paid poll workers on Election Day, helping voters and seeing democracy in action. Rules vary by state.

opportunities.title: John Locke Institute Global Essay Prize
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; scholarships and prizes for winners
opportunities.description: Global essay competition for students under 19. Entrants answer a challenging question in philosophy, politics, economics, history, psychology, theology, or law in 2,000 words or fewer.

opportunities.title: The Concord Review
opportunities.costNote: Submission fee
opportunities.description: The only quarterly journal that publishes academic history research papers written by high school students. Publication is a highly respected signal of serious independent research.

opportunities.title: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
opportunities.costNote: Paid stipend; check current age and grade rules
opportunities.description: Summer biomedical research internships in NIH labs alongside leading scientists. NIH has recently changed how high school students apply, so check the current eligibility rules (age and grade) on the NIH training site before applying.

opportunities.title: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
opportunities.costNote: No tuition; participants receive a minimum stipend
opportunities.description: Eight-week research program where high school juniors and seniors work in Stanford medical labs in areas like immunology, neuroscience, cancer biology, and bioengineering.

opportunities.title: Stanford Medical Youth Science Program (SMYSP)
opportunities.costNote: Free residential program
opportunities.description: Free five-week residential program for low-income and first-generation high school juniors from Northern and Central California who are interested in science and medicine.

opportunities.title: HOSA-Future Health Professionals
opportunities.costNote: Membership dues through your school chapter
opportunities.description: Student organization for future health professionals. Members compete in events like medical terminology, clinical skills, and health career exploration, from regional to international levels.

opportunities.title: Fred Hutch Summer High School Internship Program
opportunities.costNote: Paid internship
opportunities.description: Paid eight-week research internship for Greater Seattle students entering their senior year. Students learn lab safety and techniques, then spend six weeks in a Fred Hutch research group. No prior research experience is required.

opportunities.title: teen Mental Health First Aid
opportunities.costNote: Usually free to students through a participating school
opportunities.description: Training that teaches high school students how to recognize signs of mental health and substance use challenges in friends and how to connect them with a trusted adult.

opportunities.title: Red Cross First Aid, CPR & Lifeguard Training
opportunities.costNote: Course fees vary
opportunities.description: Certifications in first aid, CPR/AED, babysitting, and lifeguarding. Useful for summer jobs and a strong foundation for students interested in healthcare.

opportunities.title: AAMC Students & Applicants Resources
opportunities.costNote: Free online resources
opportunities.description: Free guidance from the organization behind the MCAT on what it takes to become a doctor, including career exploration, the path through college, and how medical school admissions work.

opportunities.title: ExploreHealthCareers.org
opportunities.costNote: Free online resource
opportunities.description: A free guide to more than 100 health careers, from nursing and pharmacy to public health and physical therapy, with education requirements, salaries, and summer program listings.

opportunities.title: CDC Museum Disease Detective Camp
opportunities.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
opportunities.costNote: Free day camp
opportunities.description: Free day camp for rising juniors and seniors that introduces public health and epidemiology through outbreak investigations, lab activities, and conversations with CDC scientists.

opportunities.title: Health Career Explorer Posts (Exploring)
opportunities.costNote: Small registration fee
opportunities.description: Career exploration program for ages 14-20 run with local hospitals, EMS agencies, and health organizations, giving hands-on experience with professionals in the field.

opportunities.title: USA Brain Bee
opportunities.costNote: Free or low cost locally; cash prizes at nationals
opportunities.deadline: Local competitions in winter and early spring
opportunities.description: The national neuroscience competition for students ages 13-19. Students study the brain, compete at local chapter events, and top finishers advance to the national championship and the International Brain Bee.

opportunities.title: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
opportunities.costNote: No program fee; need-based stipends may be available
opportunities.description: Mentored biomedical research program where high school juniors and seniors (16+) work in teams modeled on a Rockefeller lab, design experiments with scientist-mentors, and present their findings.

opportunities.title: MSK HOPP Summer Student Program
opportunities.costNote: Stipend after completing the program; strong science grades expected
opportunities.description: Eight-week cancer research program in MSK's Human Oncology and Pathogenesis Program. Students learn lab techniques, complete an independent project with a mentor, and present a poster. Students from disadvantaged backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

opportunities.title: UCSF Summer Student Research Program
opportunities.costNote: No tuition; check the site for current stipend details
opportunities.description: About nine weeks of mentored research in UCSF clinics and basic science labs, with workshops, seminars, and a closing research symposium. Prioritizes students from backgrounds underrepresented in science.

opportunities.title: Fred Hutch Pathways Research Explorers
opportunities.costNote: Participant costs are covered
opportunities.description: Two-week introduction to cancer research for rising 10th and 11th graders who have completed high school biology, with hands-on lab work, conversations with scientists, and a final project. Focused on students from groups excluded from biomedical careers.

opportunities.title: Area Health Education Center (AHEC) Health Careers Programs
opportunities.costNote: Usually free or low cost; varies by state
opportunities.description: State Area Health Education Centers run health career camps, job shadowing, mentoring, and clinical exposure programs for high school students, with a focus on rural, underserved, and underrepresented communities.

opportunities.title: FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid)
opportunities.costNote: Always free; never pay to file
opportunities.deadline: Opens October 1 for the next school year; state deadlines vary
opportunities.description: The single most important form for paying for college. Filing the FAFSA unlocks federal Pell Grants, work-study, and loans, and many states and colleges use it to award their own aid.

opportunities.title: CareerOneStop Scholarship Finder
opportunities.costNote: Free search tool
opportunities.description: A free, government-run search tool covering thousands of scholarships, fellowships, and grants. A safe alternative to sites that charge fees.

opportunities.title: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
opportunities.costNote: Achievement-based college scholarship
opportunities.description: Achievement-based scholarship for high school seniors who demonstrate leadership, service, and impact in their schools and communities. 150 scholars are selected each year.

opportunities.title: The Gates Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Last-dollar scholarship covering the full cost of attendance
opportunities.description: Highly selective, last-dollar scholarship for outstanding, Pell-eligible minority high school seniors with significant financial need, covering the full cost of attendance not met by other aid.

opportunities.title: QuestBridge National College Match
opportunities.costNote: Full four-year scholarships at partner colleges
opportunities.description: Connects high-achieving seniors from low-income backgrounds with full four-year scholarships to top colleges and universities through an early-decision-style match.

opportunities.title: QuestBridge College Prep Scholars
opportunities.costNote: Free; awards include college admissions support and prizes
opportunities.description: For high-achieving juniors from low-income backgrounds. Scholars receive college admissions support, invitations to college visits and conferences, and a head start on the National College Match.

opportunities.title: Jack Kent Cooke College Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Large multi-year scholarship plus advising
opportunities.description: One of the largest undergraduate scholarships in the country, for high-achieving seniors with financial need. Includes college planning support and ongoing advising.

opportunities.title: Dell Scholars Program
opportunities.costNote: Scholarship plus a laptop, textbook credits, and support
opportunities.description: For Pell-eligible seniors who have participated in an approved college readiness program. Values grit and determination over perfect grades, with wraparound support through college.

opportunities.title: Horatio Alger National Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: College scholarship for students with critical financial need
opportunities.deadline: October (for juniors applying ahead of senior year)
opportunities.description: For students who have overcome significant adversity, have critical financial need, and are involved in community service. Includes national and state-level awards.

opportunities.title: Ron Brown Scholar Program
opportunities.costNote: Four-year scholarship plus mentoring
opportunities.description: For academically talented Black high school seniors who show leadership and a commitment to community service, with lifelong mentoring and networking.

opportunities.title: Jackie Robinson Foundation Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Four-year scholarship plus mentoring
opportunities.description: For minority high school seniors with financial need and leadership potential, combining four years of funding with mentoring, internships, and leadership training.

opportunities.title: Elks Most Valuable Student Competition
opportunities.costNote: Hundreds of scholarships awarded each year
opportunities.description: Seniors are judged on scholarship, leadership, and financial need, starting at the local Elks lodge and advancing to state and national levels.

opportunities.title: Burger King Scholars
opportunities.costNote: College scholarships of varying amounts
opportunities.description: Scholarships for graduating seniors based on GPA, work experience, extracurricular involvement, community service, and financial need.

opportunities.title: National Merit Scholarship Program
opportunities.costNote: Enter by taking the PSAT/NMSQT in junior year
opportunities.deadline: PSAT/NMSQT in October of junior year
opportunities.description: Students enter by taking the PSAT/NMSQT as juniors. High scorers can become Semifinalists and Finalists, and compete for National Merit and corporate- or college-sponsored scholarships.

opportunities.title: Hispanic Scholarship Fund
opportunities.costNote: Merit-based scholarships plus support services
opportunities.description: Scholarships and support services for students of Hispanic heritage planning to enroll in college full-time, with mentoring and career resources.

opportunities.title: UNCF Scholarships
opportunities.costNote: Many scholarships with different criteria
opportunities.description: UNCF administers hundreds of scholarship programs, many for students attending historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs). Search by eligibility on their site.

opportunities.title: APIA Scholars
opportunities.organization: Asian & Pacific Islander American Scholarship Fund
opportunities.costNote: Scholarships plus leadership programming
opportunities.description: The nation's largest nonprofit providing college scholarships to Asian American and Pacific Islander students, with priority for those with financial need.

opportunities.title: American Indian College Fund Scholarships
opportunities.costNote: Scholarships for Native American and Alaska Native students
opportunities.description: Scholarships for American Indian and Alaska Native students attending tribal colleges and other accredited institutions, with one application for many awards.

opportunities.title: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Large scholarships for exceptional projects
opportunities.description: Awards students 18 and under who have completed a significant piece of work in STEM, literature, music, or philosophy that has the potential to benefit society.

opportunities.title: Coolidge Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Full-tuition, merit-based scholarship
opportunities.description: A full-ride, merit-based scholarship for high school juniors with an interest in public policy, economics, and public service, usable at any accredited U.S. college.

opportunities.title: Cameron Impact Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Four-year, full-tuition merit scholarship
opportunities.description: Full-tuition scholarship for seniors who show leadership, community service, and impact, along with strong academics.

opportunities.title: Equitable Excellence Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Scholarships for graduating seniors
opportunities.description: Recognizes seniors who demonstrate ambition, self-drive, and a commitment to making a difference in their communities.

opportunities.title: Posse Foundation Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Full-tuition leadership scholarships at partner colleges
opportunities.deadline: Nominations by schools and community organizations in the fall of senior year
opportunities.description: Identifies students with extraordinary leadership potential who may be overlooked by traditional admissions and sends them to top colleges in supportive teams, or posses.

opportunities.title: Morehead-Cain Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Covers all four years at UNC plus summer enrichment
opportunities.description: The first merit scholarship program in the U.S., covering the full cost of attendance at UNC-Chapel Hill plus funded summer experiences.

opportunities.title: Robertson Scholars Leadership Program
opportunities.costNote: Full scholarship plus funded summer experiences
opportunities.description: Full scholarship for students at Duke or UNC-Chapel Hill with full access to both campuses and three funded summer experiences.

opportunities.title: Stamps Scholars Program
opportunities.costNote: Merit scholarships with enrichment funds at partner schools
opportunities.description: Merit scholarships at dozens of partner universities that typically cover tuition and fees, plus enrichment funds for study abroad, research, or other experiences.

opportunities.title: VFW Voice of Democracy
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; college scholarships for winners
opportunities.description: Students write and record an audio essay on a patriotic theme, competing at local, state, and national levels for college scholarships.

opportunities.title: Society of Women Engineers Scholarships
opportunities.costNote: Many scholarships for future engineers
opportunities.description: Scholarships for women and gender-diverse students planning to study engineering, computer science, or engineering technology in college.

opportunities.title: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Scholarship plus a paid internship offer
opportunities.description: For seniors from underserved and historically underrepresented communities planning to study computer science, including a scholarship and a paid internship at Amazon.

opportunities.title: Live Más Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Passion-based scholarships; no grades or essays required
opportunities.description: Passion-based scholarship for ages 16-26: applicants submit a short video about their passion and goals instead of transcripts or essays.

opportunities.title: Boys & Girls Clubs Youth of the Year
opportunities.costNote: Free for club members; scholarships at state and national levels
opportunities.description: Club members ages 14-18 are honored for leadership, service, and academic excellence, competing at local, state, regional, and national levels for scholarships.

opportunities.title: Air Force ROTC High School Scholarship
opportunities.costNote: Tuition scholarship with a service commitment after graduation
opportunities.description: Merit-based scholarships that cover college tuition for students who commit to serving as Air Force or Space Force officers after graduation.

opportunities.title: Upward Bound (TRIO)
opportunities.costNote: Free; many programs include a small stipend
opportunities.description: Federally funded program for students from low-income families or who would be first-generation college students, with tutoring, summer programs on college campuses, and help applying to college.

opportunities.title: College Possible
opportunities.costNote: Free coaching
opportunities.description: Free near-peer coaching for students from low-income backgrounds on test prep, college applications, financial aid, and the transition to college.

opportunities.title: LEDA Scholars Program
opportunities.organization: Leadership Enterprise for a Diverse America
opportunities.costNote: Free, including a summer institute
opportunities.description: Free program for high-achieving juniors from low-income and underrepresented backgrounds, with a summer institute and college admissions advising through senior year.

opportunities.title: SEO Scholars
opportunities.location: New York City and San Francisco Bay Area
opportunities.costNote: Free eight-year program
opportunities.description: Free eight-year program that starts in 9th grade, providing academic coaching, mentoring, and college and career support for students from low-income families.

opportunities.title: Free Official SAT and AP Practice
opportunities.costNote: Free
opportunities.description: Free official digital SAT practice tests through College Board's Bluebook app and personalized practice on Khan Academy. Fee waivers are available for eligible students.

opportunities.title: American Red Cross Youth Volunteering
opportunities.costNote: Free
opportunities.description: Volunteer with your local Red Cross through blood drives, disaster preparedness education, and school Red Cross clubs. Great for building service hours and leadership.

opportunities.title: Habitat for Humanity Youth Programs
opportunities.costNote: Free to volunteer locally
opportunities.description: Students ages 5-25 can help build and repair homes, fundraise, and advocate for affordable housing through local affiliates and high school campus chapters. Build-site age rules vary.

opportunities.title: DoSomething.org Campaigns
opportunities.costNote: Free; some campaigns offer scholarship entries
opportunities.description: Join youth-led campaigns for social change on issues like mental health, the environment, and voting. Many campaigns include scholarship opportunities for participants.

opportunities.title: Key Club International
opportunities.costNote: Small annual dues
opportunities.description: The oldest and largest student-led service organization for high school students, focused on community service, leadership development, and character building.

opportunities.title: Interact Clubs
opportunities.costNote: Usually free; sponsored by local Rotary clubs
opportunities.description: Service clubs for ages 12-18 sponsored by Rotary. Members plan local and international service projects and develop leadership skills.

opportunities.title: Rotary Youth Exchange
opportunities.costNote: Costs vary by district; housing and meals provided by hosts
opportunities.description: Students ages 15-19 spend a few weeks or a full year abroad living with host families and attending school, building global understanding and a new language.

opportunities.title: AmeriCorps NCCC
opportunities.costNote: Living allowance, housing, and an education award after service
opportunities.description: Full-time team-based national service for ages 18-26 responding to disasters, building trails, and supporting communities. Members earn an education award toward college.

opportunities.title: Best Buddies High School Chapters
opportunities.costNote: Free to join a school chapter
opportunities.description: Build one-to-one friendships with peers who have intellectual and developmental disabilities, and lead inclusion efforts in your school.

opportunities.title: Special Olympics Unified Champion Schools
opportunities.costNote: Free for students
opportunities.description: Students with and without intellectual disabilities play on Unified Sports teams and lead inclusive youth leadership activities at school.

opportunities.title: Girl Up Clubs
opportunities.costNote: Free to start or join a club
opportunities.description: Youth-led clubs that advance gender equality through advocacy, fundraising, and leadership training, with an annual leadership summit.

opportunities.title: EarthEcho International Youth Programs
opportunities.costNote: Free
opportunities.description: Environmental programs for young people, including the EarthEcho Water Challenge and a Youth Leadership Council for teens working to protect water and oceans.

opportunities.title: Project Green Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Free; prizes and a trip to the finals for top participants
opportunities.description: A 30-day environmental challenge each October for students ages 13-25, with daily sustainability actions. Finalists attend an eco-summit.

opportunities.title: Brower Youth Awards
opportunities.costNote: Free to apply; cash award for winners
opportunities.description: Honors young environmental leaders ages 13-22 in North America for outstanding activism and achievement, with a cash prize and support for their work.

opportunities.title: Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes
opportunities.costNote: Free to apply; winners receive a cash award
opportunities.description: Celebrates young people ages 8-18 who have made a significant positive difference to people, their communities, or the environment.

opportunities.title: Paradigm Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; cash prizes
opportunities.description: Annual competition for ages 4-18 to use creativity, kindness, and science to help solve real-world problems, with a different focus each year.

opportunities.title: VolunteerMatch
opportunities.location: Online search for local and virtual roles
opportunities.costNote: Free
opportunities.description: Search thousands of local and virtual volunteer opportunities by cause and location. Filter for roles open to teens to build service hours around your interests.

opportunities.title: Volunteer at Your Local Food Bank
opportunities.costNote: Free; age requirements vary by site
opportunities.description: Find your local Feeding America food bank to sort and pack food, help at distributions, or run a food drive at school.

opportunities.title: Leo Clubs
opportunities.costNote: Low or no dues; sponsored by local Lions clubs
opportunities.description: Youth service clubs sponsored by Lions Clubs, where members plan service projects on hunger, vision, the environment, and more.

opportunities.title: 4-H
opportunities.costNote: Free or low cost, varies by county
opportunities.description: The nation's largest youth development organization, with hands-on projects in STEM, agriculture, civic engagement, and healthy living through local clubs.

opportunities.title: National Honor Society
opportunities.organization: National Association of Secondary School Principals
opportunities.costNote: Chapter dues vary
opportunities.description: Recognizes students for scholarship, service, leadership, and character. Members complete service projects and can apply for the NHS Scholarship.

opportunities.title: UNICEF USA Clubs
opportunities.costNote: Free to start or join
opportunities.description: Student clubs that advocate, fundraise, and educate to help UNICEF protect the rights and wellbeing of children worldwide.

opportunities.title: Amnesty International USA Student Groups
opportunities.costNote: Free
opportunities.description: Start or join a student group that campaigns for human rights through letter writing, awareness events, and advocacy.

opportunities.title: NASA OSTEM Internships
opportunities.costNote: Paid internships; students must be at least 16 and U.S. citizens
opportunities.deadline: Varies by session (summer usually due in late winter)
opportunities.description: Hands-on internships with NASA scientists and engineers in research, engineering, IT, and mission operations. Summer, fall, and spring sessions are offered across NASA centers, with some remote projects.

opportunities.title: Research Science Institute (RSI)
opportunities.organization: Center for Excellence in Education & MIT
opportunities.costNote: Free of charge, including housing and meals
opportunities.description: Six-week summer program at MIT where rising seniors complete coursework in scientific theory and conduct an individual research project with a mentor, then present results in written and oral form. Among the most selective programs in the country.

opportunities.title: MITES Summer
opportunities.costNote: Free, including travel, housing, and meals
opportunities.description: Rigorous six-week residential program at MIT for rising seniors, especially those from underrepresented and underserved communities. Students take college-level courses in math, physics, life sciences, and a project-based elective.

opportunities.title: MITES Semester
opportunities.costNote: Free online program
opportunities.description: A free six-month online program from MIT for high school juniors. Students take STEM courses taught by MIT-affiliated instructors and get admissions and career guidance, all while staying at home.

opportunities.title: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute
opportunities.costNote: No tuition; students complete a free online prerequisite course
opportunities.description: Four-week project-based engineering program for rising seniors. Teams build autonomous racecars, drones, satellites, and AI systems. Admission depends partly on completing an online prerequisite course.

opportunities.title: MIT PRIMES-USA
opportunities.costNote: Free year-long program
opportunities.description: Year-long remote mathematics research program for high school students who live outside the Boston area. Students work with MIT-affiliated mentors on original research problems in math.

opportunities.title: Ross Mathematics Program
opportunities.location: Columbus, OH and Terre Haute, IN
opportunities.costNote: Tuition-based with need-based financial aid
opportunities.description: Six-week immersive summer program in number theory for mathematically motivated teens ages 15-18. Students learn to think like mathematicians by working through challenging problem sets and proofs.

opportunities.title: PROMYS
opportunities.costNote: Need-based aid available; free for many families
opportunities.description: Six-week residential program focused on number theory and mathematical exploration for ambitious high school students. Participants tackle open-ended problem sets and attend lectures from mathematicians.

opportunities.title: Canada/USA Mathcamp
opportunities.costNote: Generous need-based financial aid
opportunities.description: Five-week summer program for mathematically talented students ages 13-18. Campers choose from a wide range of classes taught by mathematicians and explore topics far beyond the school curriculum.

opportunities.title: Summer Science Program (SSP)
opportunities.costNote: Need-based aid; many students attend free
opportunities.description: Five-week residential research experience in astrophysics, biochemistry, or genomics. Teams of students collect real data and complete a research project, such as determining the orbit of a near-Earth asteroid.

opportunities.title: Simons Summer Research Program
opportunities.costNote: Participants receive a stipend at the end of the program
opportunities.description: Rising seniors join Stony Brook faculty research groups in science, math, or engineering for seven weeks, complete a research abstract, and present a poster at a closing symposium.

opportunities.title: Regeneron Science Talent Search
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; large scholarship awards for top finishers
opportunities.description: The nation's oldest and most prestigious science and math competition for high school seniors. Students submit an original independent research project; top scholars and finalists receive significant awards.

opportunities.title: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
opportunities.costNote: Qualify through a local or state affiliated fair; prizes and scholarships available
opportunities.deadline: Varies by local affiliated fair (usually winter)
opportunities.description: The world's largest pre-college science competition. Students advance from school, regional, and state fairs to present independent research projects in more than 20 categories.

opportunities.title: Junior Science & Humanities Symposium (JSHS)
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; scholarship awards at regional and national levels
opportunities.description: Students present original research in STEM at regional symposia, with top presenters advancing to a national symposium. A strong option for students doing independent or mentored research.

opportunities.title: Congressional App Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter
opportunities.description: Members of Congress host app competitions in their districts. Students code an original app individually or in teams of up to four; winners are recognized by their representative and featured at the U.S. Capitol.

opportunities.title: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
opportunities.costNote: Free online contests
opportunities.description: Online programming contests in Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Platinum divisions. Strong performers are invited to a training camp that selects the U.S. team for the International Olympiad in Informatics.

opportunities.title: picoCTF
opportunities.costNote: Free; practice challenges available year-round
opportunities.description: Free cybersecurity capture-the-flag competition and learning platform from Carnegie Mellon. Students solve hacking challenges in cryptography, web exploitation, and forensics, with beginner-friendly practice problems.

opportunities.title: CyberPatriot
opportunities.location: National (teams through schools and youth groups)
opportunities.costNote: Team registration fee; waivers available for many teams
opportunities.description: National youth cyber defense competition. Teams secure virtual networks and fix vulnerabilities in timed rounds, building real cybersecurity skills with a coach and mentor.

opportunities.title: FIRST Robotics Competition
opportunities.costNote: Team fees; most teams fundraise or get sponsors
opportunities.deadline: Join a team in the fall; season kicks off in January
opportunities.description: Teams of high school students design, build, and program industrial-size robots to compete in a new game each year, while also running their team like a business. Opens doors to FIRST scholarships.

opportunities.title: FIRST Tech Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Team fees; grants available for new teams
opportunities.deadline: Join a team in the fall
opportunities.description: Teams design, build, and code smaller robots with a reusable kit to compete in an alliance-based game. More accessible and affordable than FRC while still building real engineering skills.

opportunities.title: VEX Robotics Competition
opportunities.costNote: Team registration and kit costs; grants available
opportunities.description: Student teams design and build robots to play a yearly engineering game against other teams, from local tournaments up to the VEX Robotics World Championship.

opportunities.title: Science Olympiad
opportunities.costNote: Teams register through schools
opportunities.description: Team competition with 23 events spanning biology, earth science, chemistry, physics, engineering, and technology. Teams advance from regional and state tournaments to nationals.

opportunities.title: American Mathematics Competitions (AMC 10/12)
opportunities.costNote: Small registration fee through your school or a host site
opportunities.description: The first step toward the USA Mathematical Olympiad. High scorers on the AMC 10 or 12 qualify for the AIME and beyond. A great signal of math talent for colleges.

opportunities.title: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO)
opportunities.costNote: School registration fee
opportunities.deadline: School registration in fall; open exam in winter
opportunities.description: National biology competition. Top scorers on the open and semifinal exams attend a national finals camp, where four students are chosen for the International Biology Olympiad team.

opportunities.title: U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad
opportunities.costNote: Organized through ACS local sections
opportunities.description: Multi-tiered chemistry competition. Students start with a local exam, advance to a national exam, and the top 20 attend a study camp to choose the U.S. International Chemistry Olympiad team.

opportunities.title: U.S. Physics Team (F=ma and USAPhO)
opportunities.costNote: School registration fee
opportunities.description: The F=ma exam leads to the USA Physics Olympiad; top performers join a training camp that selects the U.S. team for the International Physics Olympiad.

opportunities.title: NASA International Space Apps Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Free to participate
opportunities.description: A global two-day hackathon where teams use NASA's open data to solve real challenges on Earth and in space. Open to all ages, with local events and a virtual option.

opportunities.title: Army Educational Outreach Program (AEOP) Apprenticeships
opportunities.costNote: Paid stipend for apprentices
opportunities.description: Summer research apprenticeships (such as REAP and HSAP) that place high school students in university and Army research labs with mentors. REAP prioritizes students from groups historically underrepresented in STEM.

opportunities.title: Science and Engineering Apprenticeship Program (SEAP)
opportunities.organization: U.S. Navy / Office of Naval Research
opportunities.costNote: Paid stipend; must be at least 16 and a U.S. citizen
opportunities.description: Eight-week summer research internships at Navy laboratories, where students work alongside scientists and engineers on real defense research projects.

opportunities.title: ACS Project SEED
opportunities.costNote: Paid fellowship for students from low-income households
opportunities.description: Paid summer research experiences in chemistry and related fields for students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds, mentored by scientists in academic, industry, and government labs.

opportunities.title: Girls Who Code Summer Pathways
opportunities.costNote: Free; need-based grants for technology and internet
opportunities.description: Free, virtual, self-paced summer program for high school girls and nonbinary students, with tracks such as web development, data science and AI, game design, and cybersecurity. No prior coding experience required.

opportunities.title: Kode With Klossy Summer Camps
opportunities.costNote: Free coding camps
opportunities.description: Free two-week coding camps for students ages 13-18 who are women, trans, or nonbinary. Tracks include web development, mobile apps, and data science.

opportunities.title: Technovation Girls
opportunities.costNote: Free to participate
opportunities.deadline: Registration in fall; submissions in spring
opportunities.description: Teams of girls ages 8-18 identify a problem in their community and build a mobile or AI app to solve it, along with a business plan and pitch video.

opportunities.title: Conrad Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter
opportunities.description: Innovation and entrepreneurship competition where teams ages 13-18 develop products to solve global problems in categories like aerospace, energy, health, and cybersecurity.

opportunities.title: MIT THINK Scholars Program
opportunities.location: Online with a trip to MIT for finalists
opportunities.costNote: Free; finalists receive project funding and mentorship
opportunities.description: Students submit a proposal for a science, technology, or engineering project. Finalists receive funding, mentorship from MIT students, and a trip to MIT to build their idea.

opportunities.title: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; winner receives a large college scholarship
opportunities.description: Students ages 13-18 create a short video explaining a big idea in physics, life sciences, or mathematics. Winners receive a college scholarship, plus awards for their teacher and school.

opportunities.title: Genes in Space
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter
opportunities.description: Students in grades 7-12 propose DNA experiments that address a challenge of space exploration. The winning experiment is conducted aboard the International Space Station.

opportunities.title: MathWorks Math Modeling Challenge (M3)
opportunities.costNote: Free to enter; scholarship prizes for top teams
opportunities.deadline: Registration closes in February; challenge weekend in late winter
opportunities.description: Teams of juniors and seniors spend 14 hours using mathematical modeling to tackle a real-world problem, competing for scholarship prizes.

opportunities.title: National Youth Science Camp
opportunities.costNote: Free, including travel
opportunities.description: Free residential STEM program in West Virginia for two outstanding students from each state, with lectures from scientists, hands-on research, and outdoor adventures. Housing, meals, and travel are covered.

opportunities.title: Carnegie Mellon Summer Academy for Math + Science (SAMS)
opportunities.costNote: Free for admitted students
opportunities.description: Free summer program for rising seniors that builds college readiness in STEM, with a focus on students who are first-generation or from communities underrepresented in STEM.

opportunities.title: Carnegie Mellon Pre-College Programs
opportunities.costNote: Tuition-based with need-based aid
opportunities.description: Summer programs in computer science, AI, engineering, architecture, and the arts on CMU's campus, giving students a taste of college-level work.

opportunities.title: Johns Hopkins Engineering Innovation
opportunities.organization: Johns Hopkins Whiting School of Engineering
opportunities.costNote: Tuition-based; scholarships available
opportunities.description: College-level introduction to engineering where students solve real engineering problems and can earn Johns Hopkins college credit.

opportunities.title: Johns Hopkins Center for Talented Youth (CTY)
opportunities.costNote: Tuition-based with need-based financial aid
opportunities.description: Advanced online and summer courses in math, science, writing, and the humanities for academically talented students, with eligibility based on testing or other qualifications.

opportunities.title: Boston University RISE Internship/Practicum
opportunities.costNote: Tuition-based; financial aid available
opportunities.description: Six-week summer program where rising seniors either conduct research in a BU faculty lab (Internship track) or take a research methods course with group projects (Practicum track).

opportunities.title: NYU Tandon ARISE
opportunities.costNote: Free program for New York City students
opportunities.description: Applied Research Innovations in Science and Engineering: a free summer program for NYC high school students who join NYU research labs and complete a research project with a mentor.

opportunities.title: Jackson Laboratory Summer Student Program
opportunities.location: Bar Harbor, ME and Farmington, CT
opportunities.costNote: Paid stipend plus room and board
opportunities.description: Ten-week paid research fellowship for graduating high school seniors and undergraduates, who join JAX labs in genetics and genomics with a scientist mentor and present their work at the end of the summer.

opportunities.title: National FFA Organization
opportunities.costNote: Small membership dues through your school chapter
opportunities.deadline: Join anytime through an agricultural education program
opportunities.description: Student organization for those interested in agriculture, food science, natural resources, and agribusiness, with career development events, leadership conferences, and scholarships.

opportunities.title: SkillsUSA
opportunities.costNote: Membership dues through your school chapter
opportunities.description: Career and technical student organization for trade, technical, and skilled service careers. Members compete in more than 100 contests, from welding and robotics to culinary arts.

opportunities.title: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program
opportunities.organization: Civil Air Patrol (U.S. Air Force Auxiliary)
opportunities.costNote: Annual membership dues
opportunities.description: Youth program for ages 12-18 focused on aerospace education, leadership, and emergency services, with orientation flights and opportunities that can lead toward a pilot's license.

opportunities.title: Stanford University Mathematics Camp (SUMaC)
opportunities.costNote: Tuition with need-based financial aid
opportunities.description: Advanced summer mathematics program where students explore abstract algebra, number theory, topology, and more through lectures and research-style group work, offered residentially and online.

opportunities.title: Anson L. Clark Scholars Program
opportunities.costNote: No program fee; room and board plus a stipend ($25 application fee)
opportunities.description: Seven-week summer research program for twelve high school juniors and seniors (17+), who work one-on-one with Texas Tech faculty in science, engineering, humanities, and more.

opportunities.title: Khan Academy
opportunities.costNote: Always free
opportunities.description: Free courses and practice in math, science, computing, economics, and test prep, from algebra through AP and college-level material. Great for getting ahead or filling gaps before a competitive program.

opportunities.title: MIT OpenCourseWare
opportunities.costNote: Free, no registration required
opportunities.description: Free lecture videos, notes, and problem sets from thousands of real MIT courses, including a section designed for high school students.

opportunities.title: Harvard CS50: Introduction to Computer Science
opportunities.costNote: Free to take online; optional paid certificate
opportunities.description: Harvard's famous intro computer science course, free online. Learn programming in C, Python, SQL, and web development through lectures and hands-on problem sets, at your own pace.

opportunities.title: freeCodeCamp
opportunities.costNote: Free nonprofit curriculum and certifications
opportunities.description: A nonprofit with thousands of hours of free interactive coding lessons and projects in web development, JavaScript, Python, and data analysis, plus free certifications.
